children: The credibility of the headline figure, at 7.8%, has significantly improved. But while recent revisions address some IMF criticism, they don’t go far enough to reduce unnecessary surprises in the $4 trln economy's performance. More transparency is needed on inputs.
Full view will be published shortly.
Follow Shritama Bose on LinkedIn and X.

Former finance secretary Subhash Chandra Garg on September 2 questioned India's official GDP growth print of 7.8% for the three months to end June. A sharp official downward revision to the growth numbers in the comparable quarter of the last fiscal year makes the latest growth rate appear stronger, he argued in a column for news website Quint and in an interview with television channel NDTV.

Statistics secretary Saurabh Garg defended the estimate and large revisions to recent GDP data on the same day, saying the changes reflected the use of more granular price ​signals and additional sources rather than any systematic bias in the numbers.
